title: Letter formation & handwriting
examples: Where do I start writing the letter 'a'?
What is the difference between a capital and a small letter?
How do I make the letter 'g' without going outside the lines?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to write letters neatly. We will look at where to start each letter. Watch me write the letter 't' now.
For most letters, you start at the top line. This helps keep your writing straight and tidy. Try starting your letter 'm' at the top.
Some letters go up high, these are called ascenders. Think of the tall stick on the letter 'l'.
Some letters go down low, these are descenders. The tail of the letter 'g' is a descender. It goes below the line.
Remember that big letters are capitals, and small letters are lowercase. The capital 'A' is bigger than the small 'a'.

faq.q: Why do I have to know where to start writing letters?
faq.a: Knowing the start point helps your letters look neat. It keeps your writing consistent and easy to read. You might also ask, 'What is the right beginning for this letter?' or 'Where should my pen go first?'
asks: What is the correct starting point for a letter?
Do I always start at the top when writing?

faq.a: Ascenders are parts of letters that go up above the writing line. Descenders are parts that hang down below the writing line. You could also ask, 'Which letters go up high?' or 'What letters drop below the line?'
asks: What is a letter that goes below the line?
Can you show me an ascender letter?

faq.q: How do I know when to use a capital letter?
faq.a: You use a capital letter for the start of a sentence. You also use them for names of people and places. Another way to ask is, 'When do I use a big letter?' or 'What letter do I use for names?'
asks: When is a capital letter needed?
Do I always use a capital at the start?

faq.q: Is the capital letter always bigger than the small letter?
faq.a: Yes, generally the capital letter is much larger than its lowercase partner. This helps us tell them apart when we write. You might ask, 'Which letter is bigger?' or 'What is the difference in size?'

faq.q: What if my letter is too messy?
faq.a: If your letter is messy, try slowing down your writing speed. Focus on making the correct strokes in order. You can also ask, 'How do I make my letters neater?' or 'What should I do if I mess up?'
asks: How to improve my letter formation?

facts: Most letters start writing at the top line.
Ascenders are parts that rise above the main writing line.
Descenders drop below the main writing line.
Capitals are used for the beginning of sentences and names.

quiz.say: When writing the letter 'b', where should your pen start?
quiz.why: The letter 'b' is a standard letter that begins its strokes at the top line.

wrong.0: Starting in the middle makes the letter look unbalanced and unfinished.
wrong.1: The starting point is determined by the top boundary, not just the side.
wrong.3: This is tempting because some descenders go low, but 'b' starts at the top.

quiz.why: The letter 'g' has a tail that goes below the writing line, making it a descender.

wrong.1: The letter 'a' stays entirely on the main writing line.
wrong.2: The letter 'l' only goes up, it does not drop below the line.
wrong.3: The letter 't' only extends up, it does not drop below the line.

quiz.say: If I write my name, which letters will be capitals?

options.show: The first letter of each name
options.say: The first letter of each name

quiz.why: You must use a capital letter for the first letter of every name you write.

wrong.0: This is wrong because names always start with a capital letter.
wrong.2: You only use capitals for specific important letters, not every single one.
wrong.3: The first letter is the most important place to use a capital.
